article.title: Covert recording of prison meeting between Beau Lamarre-Condon and friend played to double murder trial

article.content: Former police officer accused of shooting dead Jesse Baird and Luke Davies apologised to friend, acknowledging ‘you’re involved because of me’ Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast A covert recording captured Beau Lamarre-Condon telling a friend during a meeting in prison in December last year, “I fully take accountability that you’re involved because of me now,” a Sydney court has heard. article.aiArticle:
A covert prison recording capturing a former police officer charged with a double murder has been played for a court, according to World news | The Guardian. During the intercepted prison meeting, the accused man offered an apology to a friend, acknowledging on the audio that the associate had been dragged into the situation because of him. The trial centers on the deaths of **Jesse Baird** and **Luke Davies**, who were allegedly shot dead. 

## Secret Prison Audio Presented in Court

The details of the covert recording emerged during court proceedings as prosecutors introduced the prison audio as evidence. According to the report, the defendant told his friend during the visit that he recognized the personal fallout and trouble the associate was facing by association. Legal teams examined the conversation closely, as the recording provides a rare, unscripted window into the mindset of the former law enforcement officer following his apprehension. Such audio captures often form a major pillar of prosecution arguments in high-profile criminal trials involving law enforcement personnel.

## Broader Context and Past Cases

High-profile murder trials involving former public servants or defense personnel frequently draw intense public scrutiny regarding institutional trust and accountability. When individuals trained by the state use those skills in alleged crimes, the legal proceedings often involve meticulous forensic examinations of post-arrest behavior, similar to cases seen in other jurisdictions where an [Australian murderer loses bid to eat Vegemite in prison](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/australian-murderer-loses-bid-to-eat-vegemite-in-prison) or where courts dissect the psychological profiles of defendants, such as a [Former RAAF pilot who allegedly murdered wife was ‘love rat’ and ‘master manipulator’, jury hears](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/former-raaf-pilot-who-allegedly-murdered-wife-was-love-rat-and-master). 

## Why This Matters

This evidence touches upon core questions of accountability, police integrity, and the emotional fallout experienced by peripheral witnesses pulled into violent crimes. For the families of **Jesse Baird** and **Luke Davies**, every piece of presented audio and testimony represents another step through a prolonged judicial process aimed at establishing accountability. The case also highlights the extent to which law enforcement agencies monitor communications of high-profile inmates to gather unvarnished insights into criminal charges. 

## What to Watch

Observers will be tracking how the defense responds to the interpretation of the covert recording during upcoming cross-examinations. The court is expected to hear further witness testimonies and legal arguments regarding the admissibility and weight of the prison audio as the trial progresses.

Sources: [World news | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/oct/26/beau-lamarre-condon-trial-covert-prison-recording-with-friend-played-to-court-ntwnfb)
